# @codenhub/validation

> Validation of untrusted input for TypeScript: formats return what the URL parser read, work and issues are bounded for hostile input, and an issue never holds the input. Each validator is a standalone function, so a package or app ships only the checks it uses. Works for a single value such as an email or a port, and for whole objects such as forms. The package is experimental.

A validator takes any input and returns `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, error: { issues } }`; it never throws for invalid input. Create one by calling a factory, then call it with the value: `email()(input)`, `number({ int: true, min: 0 })(input)`. Every factory takes its own arguments, then options, then checks, which are rules for rarer cases: `string({ min: 3 }, startsWith("a"))`. Every validator that reports an issue takes a `message` option. Ready-made validators cover strings, numbers, bigints, booleans, symbols, dates, functions, literals and enums, and formats such as email, url, domain, ip, cidr, phone, uuid, datetime, time, duration, semver, slug, jwt, creditCard and port. `url` and `email` take validators for their parts (`url({ host: hostname() })`), and `searchParams` reads a query string into typed values. Collections (`array`, `tuple`, `record`, `set`, `map`), `union`, `tagged`, `intersection`, `optional` (with an optional default), `nullable`, `transform` and `lazy` combine them. Build objects with `object`, add rules with `check`, and rules across properties that do not wait for the other properties with `checkFields`, build your own with `format` and `guard`, chain with `pipe`, and read the type a validator produces with `Infer` and the type it accepts with `InferInput`, which `is` narrows its input to. Text input is converted with the `coerce*` validators, `standard` exposes a validator as a Standard Schema, `describe` returns what a validator is made of, its kind, options, checks and the validators inside it, as plain data to walk, and `toJsonSchema` writes a validator as a JSON Schema, draft 2020-12. `pick`, `omit`, `required` and `partial` make a new object validator from one `object` made. Issues carry a code, a path and params, never the input; `formatIssue` and `flatten` turn them into text from a message map you pass, `englishMessages` for the built-in English, `portugueseMessages` for Portuguese, or your own to reword or localize. `brand(validator, name)` marks the type a validator produces, in the types alone, and `readonly(validator)` makes what it produces read-only and freezes it. A validator with an asynchronous check is an `AsyncValidator` and must be awaited.

## Documentation

- [Documentation overview](docs/index.md): The idea, results, objects, combining validators, and sync versus async.
- [Validator reference](docs/validators.md): Every validator, check and combinator with its options and the issue it reports, and the parts of `url` and `email`.
- [Custom validators](docs/custom-validators.md): Rules with `check`, validators with `format` and `guard`, asynchronous rules and testing.
- [Coercion](docs/coercion.md): `coerceString`, `coerceNumber`, `coerceBoolean`, `coerceBigint` and `coerceDate` for text input such as environment variables and form fields.
- [Standard Schema](docs/standard-schema.md): `standard(validator, messages)` for libraries that accept a Standard Schema.
- [JSON Schema](docs/json-schema.md): `toJsonSchema(validator, { io, unrepresentable })`, what each validator is written as, input against output, and what cannot be written.
- [Comparison](docs/comparison.md): How the package differs from valibot, zod and yup, what was measured, and when to choose one of them.
- [Issues and messages](docs/errors.md): The shape of an issue, built-in codes and params, message text, the `message` option, localization and form errors.
- [API reference](docs/reference/index.md): Every export with its signature and documentation, generated from the source.
- [Changelog](docs/changelog/index.md): Release notes, and the migrations from 0.1.0 and from 0.0.1.
